title: Born 4 Days Apart. One of Them Became Audrey Hepburn.
title_alternatives: Born 4 Days Apart. One of Them Became Audrey Hepburn.
Two Girls, 19km Apart. Four Weeks of Rent Decided Everything.
She Was the Better Dancer. Then the Money Ran Out.
Both Were Rejected in 1948. Only One Could Afford to Stay.
The Other Girl Taught 400 Children and Was Never Bitter
description:
In the last week of April 1929, in the same Dutch province, two girls were born four days apart. One of them was called Wil de Groot. Her father repaired bicycles. The other girl's family had a title, and her birth was noted in a newspaper.

They never met. Neither of them, as far as anybody has established, ever knew the other existed.

What makes them worth putting side by side is not the coincidence of dates, and it is certainly not the shape people expect — one life a success, the other a quiet tragedy in the background. That version is wrong.

In 1935, if you had only the school records in front of you, you would have picked Wil. She was the better reader and was moved up a year. The other girl was moved between countries instead, and lost most of a year of schooling.

In the winter of 1944 they were nineteen kilometres apart and both of them were starving. The winter did roughly the same physical damage to both. Both were left thin in a way that a certain kind of person would later call elegant in one case and undernourished in the other.

In the spring of 1948, five weeks apart, both auditioned in London. Both were rejected, for the same reason and in almost the same words: too old to train. They were nineteen.

The difference arrived after that. It was not talent and it was not character. One of them had a mother with a flat in London, and could therefore afford to still be in the city four weeks later, in a season when somebody happened to be looking. The other one went home, because the money ran out.

What Wil de Groot did with the next four decades is the other half of this story, and it involves a room above a shop, thirty-three years, and about four hundred children.

This story is a work of fiction. Wil, Annemarie, Joop and every detail in it are invented, created for storytelling and not drawn from any record.
